The formula for the derivative of the inverse hyperbolic secant function is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arsech}⁡x)=-\frac{1}{x\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}.
$$

Using the formula above with the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\,(2\,\operatorname{arsech}⁡(5x)) \\  & =2\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\,(\operatorname{arsech}⁡(5x)) \\  & =2\cdot (-\frac{1}{(5x)\sqrt{1-(5x)^{2}}})\cdot (5x)^{′} \\  & =-\frac{2}{5x\sqrt{1-25{x}^{2}}}\cdot 5 \\  & =-\frac{2}{x\sqrt{1-25{x}^{2}}}.\end{aligned}
$$
